summary: Round 9, test review. Both round-8 findings verified KILLED in my own tree, each at the right site and for the right reason. (1) The new theBOUNDEDCrossingSTOPSAtTheBarrierReachedThroughAnUncheckpointedEpoch genuinely routes through the WALK's probe, not the first hop: widening ChainReplay.java:163 `limit` to Long.MAX_VALUE fails it and nothing else, with `expected 1 but was 2` -- the zombie folded in; and widening the FIRST hop (:129) instead leaves the new test GREEN while failing only its two siblings. The two tests are disjoint and complementary, so the second call site now has its own net. (2) `assertThat(reader.nextSequence()).isEqualTo(1)` kills `if (true)` for the `chainEpoch == ownEpoch` guard at :246, failing at line 319 with `expected 1 but was 41` -- epoch 1's next slot adopted as epoch 4's. THIRD CALL SITE: nothing to test. `limit` is assigned Long.MAX_VALUE at :187 and not reassigned before :197, so `limit -> Long.MAX_VALUE` there is a syntactically equivalent mutant. The probe ITSELF at that site is netted (deleting :197-199 fails aRunOfBURNEDEpochsStillStopsAtTheCheckpointBehindThem). MULTI-CONSTRUCTION SWEEP, ten further mutants measured: killed -- startAfter off-by-one keyFor(from) (6 tests), barrier `- 1 >=` (1), dropping the first-hop tail replay (5), dropping the hop's `from` bound (5), `chainEpoch >= 1` at :163 (1), `if (true)` at :172 (2), and ADR-0035's own rejected alternative `epoch != ownEpoch &&` at :129 (6, confirming the ADR's claim). Survived -- two, both filed below, neither blocking. RULES 4-5: no assertion deleted or loosened in the delta; the only removals are the CheckpointCursor rename and the four LocalSequencerFailoverTest budget moves (28/56/20/47 -> 30/58/22/52), which are exact equalities moved upward, stated at the site and carried by ADR-0035 as cost.md R18 requires. Restored tree, `./gradlew test --rerun-tasks` BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 300 tests; repository `git diff --cached` unchanged at b94c35a05bb1.

findings.title: The epoch-0 guard on the BURNED-EPOCH probe -- new code in this commit -- has no net, and neither does its pre-existing sibling three lines below. Same shape as the round-8 blocker: one invariant, four constructions, two pinned.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer simplifying `replayAncestry` drops `chainEpoch >= 1 &&` from the burned-epoch probe at :197. MEASURED IN MY OWN TREE, not argued: `./gradlew test` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL across every module, 300 tests. The walk then probes epoch 0 -- the RESERVED unleased chain the sibling comment at :167-171 says must never be read into a leased chain's history -- costing one extra `stat` per burned-epoch recovery that descends to 0, and, if epoch 0 ever carried a checkpoint, folding the unleased chain's offsets in and stopping the walk there. Today only the cost differs, because `CheckpointWriter` is constructed at exactly one site (LocalSequencer.java:304) with a leased epoch >= 1, so the correctness leg is latent rather than live. The same guard on the CONTINUE branch is netted twice: dropping `chainEpoch >= 1 &&` at :163 fails LocalSequencerFailoverTest.aTakeoverReadsEveryEntryOfEveryANCESTORAndTHATISAREGRESSION, and `if (chainEpoch >= 1)` -> `if (true)` at :172 fails that plus CommitLogCrossEpochTest.aFirstChainNamingNoPredecessorCrossesNothing. The burned-epoch pair has no net at all -- `if (true)` at :200 is also BUILD SUCCESSFUL. The gap is that no fixture drives the arithmetic branch DOWN TO epoch 0; aRunOfBURNEDEpochsStillStopsAtTheCheckpointBehindThem stops at epoch 1's checkpoint by construction. Closing it needs a burned run reaching the origin (e.g. epoch 1 burned, epoch 2 continuing from it) with an exact request count. Minor and NOT blocking: the branch is unreachable in production today (LocalSequencer.start resolves burned epochs through firstInheritableAncestor first, as :190-196 records), the live consequence is one `stat`, and half the gap predates this commit.

findings.title: `crossFromCheckpoint`'s two `Math.max` uses are EQUIVALENT MUTANTS by construction -- so this is not a test gap, but the javadoc asserts an I2 protection the control flow already makes unreachable.
findings.failure_scenario: Both measured BUILD SUCCESSFUL: `offsets.merge(key, at.nextOffset(), Math::max)` -> `offsets.put(key, at.nextOffset())` at :245, and `nextSequence = Math.max(nextSequence, checkpoint.sequence())` -> `nextSequence = checkpoint.sequence()` at :253. I am explicitly NOT calling these weak tests: `crossFromCheckpoint` can succeed at most once per `ChainReplay` instance (every caller breaks or returns on true) and always runs BEFORE any `applyChain` (the apply loop is at :212, after the while), so `offsets` is empty and `nextSequence` is 0 at that point. No test can distinguish them; that is the definition of an equivalent mutant. What IS reportable is the method javadoc at :230-232 -- 'THE OFFSETS ARE MERGED, not assigned ... taking the later value unconditionally would rewind the stream (I2)' -- which describes a hazard this method's own control flow forecloses. A maintainer reading it believes a live I2 guard sits here. The failure that follows: someone reorders the apply loop before the probe, or adds a second successful probe (M4.23's origin walk is the named candidate), the sentence becomes load-bearing for the first time, and no test in the tree can tell whether it still holds -- the same 'code no test can distinguish from a no-op' shape this commit's own recoveringAChainThatCheckpointedItsOWNProgressKeepsItsNextSequence cites as the reason to pin rather than delete, except here it cannot be pinned. The remedy is one clause saying the merge is FORWARD DEFENCE against a second probe rather than a live guard, not another test. Production reviewer's call as much as mine; minor, not blocking, and fixing it in round 9 is probably the wrong trade under rule 11.
